newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iraqi U.N. envoy criticises Albright speech.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi U.N. envoy criticises Albright speech.

text.p: Iraq said on Thursday a recent speech by U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright contained "sophistries and distortions of fact" and reflected a contempt for Security Council resolutions.

In a letter to the president of the council, Iraqi U.N. Ambassador Nizar Hamdoon quoted Albright as saying in a March 26 speech at Georgetown University in Washington, "We do not agree with those nations that say that if Iraq complies with its obligations relating to weapons of mass destruction then the sanctions must be lifted."

"This statement is contrary to the provisions of paragraph 22 of Security Council Resolution 687 (1991)," Hamdoon said, referring to conditions for lifting sanctions imposed on Iraq soon after its August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

"With this statement, Ms. Albright has frankly admitted the covert United States plan to exploit the machinery of Chapter VII of the Charter in order to settle accounts with Iraq," he said, referring to the U.N. Charter's enforcement provisions.
As the United States U.N. representative, before becoming secretary of state earlier this year, Albright played a key role in maintaining sanctions against Iraq.

Saying she also "spoke at length of the kind of new regime she would like in Iraq," Hamdoon said this was "incompatible with the principles of international law and the Charter of the United Nations as they relate to non-interference in the internal affairs of states."

Taking issue with a statement by Albright that she had no differences at all with the people of Iraq, Hamdoon quoted her as saying during a May 1996 television interview that sanctions were "worth the price" of the deaths of more than half a million Iraqi children.
He described as "obviously absurd" a statement by the secretary of state that the deployment of U.S. forces in the region was "a precaution against further miscalculations on the part of Iraq."
"The reason for the deployment of United States forces is to control the region and its resources and to usurp the will of its peoples," he said.

Hamdoon said Albright's warning of the dangers Iraq posed to security in the region came at a time when the United States used its Security Council veto twice to block resolutions opposing Israel's construction of settlements in occupied territories.

"This once again reveals the use of double standards in United States foreign policy and the fact that that policy places the interests of the United States and Israel above international law, the Charter of the United Nations and the resolutions of the Security Council," he said.
